subproblem.title: Integrals converge if they converge on every piece of a countable measurable partition, under integrable domination (Tannery)
subproblem.statement: Let X be a measurable space, ν a measure on X, V_j ⊆ X (j ∈ ℕ) measurable and pairwise disjoint with ν(X ∖ ⋃_j V_j) = 0, b : X → ℝ ν-integrable, F_k : X → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) ν-integrable with |F_k(x)| ≤ b(x) for ν-a.e. x (for every k), and F_∞ : X → ℝ ν-integrable. If ∫_{V_j} F_k dν → ∫_{V_j} F_∞ dν as k → ∞ for every j, then ∫_X F_k dν → ∫_X F_∞ dν as k → ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [MeasurableSpace X] (ν : Measure X) (V : ℕ → Set X) (b : X → ℝ) (F : ℕ → X → ℝ) (Flim : X → ℝ), (∀ j, MeasurableSet (V j)) → Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint V) → ν (⋃ j, V j)ᶜ = 0 → Integrable b ν → (∀ k, Integrable (F k) ν) → (∀ k, ∀ᵐ x ∂ν, ‖F k x‖ ≤ b x) → Integrable Flim ν → (∀ j, Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x in V j, F k x ∂ν) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x in V j, Flim x ∂ν))) → Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x, F k x ∂ν) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, Flim x ∂ν))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (countable additivity of the integral over the disjoint chart pieces, then dominated convergence for series), stated for an abstract measure. Notation: Fl := F_∞; all integrals are Bochner integrals and ∫_V H dν := ∫ H d(ν⌞V).
1. (ν lives on ⋃_j V_j.) The set (⋃_j V_j)ᶜ is ν-null, i.e. ν-a.e. x lies in ⋃_j V_j. Hence ν⌞(⋃_j V_j) = ν (Mathlib `Measure.restrict_eq_self_of_ae_mem`, after rewriting with `ae_iff`).
2. (Countable additivity.) Let H : X → ℝ be ν-integrable. Then H is integrable on ⋃_j V_j, and because the V_j are measurable and pairwise disjoint, the series Σ_j ∫_{V_j} H dν converges with sum ∫_{⋃_j V_j} H dν (Mathlib `hasSum_integral_iUnion`). By step 1 this sum is ∫_X H dν. So HasSum (j ↦ ∫_{V_j} H dν) (∫_X H dν).
3. (Summable majorant.) Step 2 for H = b shows that B_j := ∫_{V_j} b dν is summable. For all k, j: |∫_{V_j} F_k dν| ≤ ∫_{V_j} |F_k| dν ≤ ∫_{V_j} b dν = B_j. The first inequality is `norm_integral_le_integral_norm`. The second is monotonicity of the integral (`integral_mono_ae`): |F_k| and b are integrable on V_j, and |F_k| ≤ b holds ν-a.e., hence ν⌞V_j-a.e. (`ae_restrict_of_ae`).
4. (Tannery's theorem.) Let a_k(j), a(j) ∈ ℝ with a_k(j) → a(j) as k → ∞ for every j, and |a_k(j)| ≤ B_j for all k, j, where Σ_j B_j < ∞. Then Σ_j a_k(j) → Σ_j a(j).
Proof. First, |a(j)| ≤ B_j by passing to the limit, so all series converge absolutely. Given ε > 0, choose a finite set T ⊆ ℕ with Σ_{j∉T} B_j < ε/3. Choose k₀ with |Σ_{j∈T}(a_k(j) − a(j))| < ε/3 for k ≥ k₀; this is a finite sum of convergent sequences. For k ≥ k₀,
|Σ_j a_k(j) − Σ_j a(j)| ≤ |Σ_{j∈T}(a_k(j) − a(j))| + Σ_{j∉T}|a_k(j)| + Σ_{j∉T}|a(j)| < ε.
This is Mathlib's `tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence` (Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/Tannery.lean). That file is not in the import closure of GMT.Ch06.Submission, so inline this ε/3 argument as a local `have` for f : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ along `atTop`; Mathlib's proof compiles verbatim with the existing imports. Adding `import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Group.Tannery` to Submission.lean is an alternative.
5. (Conclusion.) Put a_k(j) := ∫_{V_j} F_k dν and a(j) := ∫_{V_j} Fl dν. The hypothesis gives a_k(j) → a(j) for every j, and step 3 gives |a_k(j)| ≤ B_j with Σ_j B_j < ∞. By step 4, Σ_j a_k(j) → Σ_j a(j). Step 2, applied to H = F_k and to H = Fl (both ν-integrable), gives Σ_j a_k(j) = ∫_X F_k dν for every k and Σ_j a(j) = ∫_X Fl dν (`HasSum.tsum_eq`). Hence ∫_X F_k dν → ∫_X Fl dν. ∎
proof_key_steps: ν is concentrated on ⋃_j V_j, so ∫_X H dν = Σ_j ∫_{V_j} H dν for every ν-integrable H (hasSum_integral_iUnion).
|∫_{V_j} F_k dν| ≤ B_j := ∫_{V_j} b dν, and Σ_j B_j = ∫_X b dν < ∞.
Tannery's theorem (dominated convergence for series, ε/3 argument) gives Σ_j ∫_{V_j} F_k dν → Σ_j ∫_{V_j} F_∞ dν.
Both series equal the full integrals ∫_X F_k dν and ∫_X F_∞ dν.

subproblem.title: Chain rule on a C¹ chart for a Lipschitz function with a tangential gradient: D(h∘Φ)(w) = ⟨G(Φ(w)), DΦ(w)·⟩ a.e.
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, and Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P of class C¹, Lipschitz on Ω and κ-antilipschitz on Ω for some κ > 0. Let A ⊆ ℝ^P be Hⁿ-null-measurable, h : ℝ^P → ℝ L-Lipschitz and G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P. Suppose that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A, every w ∈ Ω with Φ(w) = x and every u ∈ range DΦ(w), the function s ↦ h(x + su) has derivative ⟨G(x), u⟩ at s = 0. Then for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A), h∘Φ is Fréchet differentiable at w with derivative s ↦ ⟨G(Φ(w)), DΦ(w)s⟩, i.e. the continuous linear map (innerSL ℝ (G(Φ(w)))) ∘ DΦ(w). Here Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P, Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ and DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (A : Set (Eucl P)) (h : Eucl P → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0) (G : Eucl P → Eucl P), IsOpen Ω → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → (∃ K : ℝ≥0, LipschitzOnWith K Φ Ω) → (∃ κ : ℝ, 0 < κ ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, κ * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → NullMeasurableSet A (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → LipschitzWith L h → (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict A), ∀ w ∈ Ω, Φ w = x → ∀ u ∈ LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w).toLinearMap, HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => h (x + s • u)) (inner ℝ (G x) u) 0) → ∀ᵐ w ∂((volume : Measure (Eucl n)).restrict (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' A)), HasFDerivAt (h ∘ Φ) ((innerSL ℝ (G (Φ w))).comp (fderiv ℝ Φ w)) w
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 7(c),(d) and 9(b) of the parent proof: Rademacher on the chart, the directional-derivative fact (Simon Ch. 2, 4.10), and uniqueness of derivatives. Notation: D := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A), A_w := DΦ(w), and K is a Lipschitz constant of Φ on Ω.
1. (Pulling back the hypothesis.) Let p(x) be the property: 'for every w ∈ Ω with Φ(w) = x and every u ∈ range A_w, s ↦ h(x + su) has derivative ⟨G(x), u⟩ at 0'. Apply the sibling ae_pullback (lpf_ccr_ae_pullback) with M := A. Its hypotheses hold: Ω is open, hence measurable; Φ is continuous (C¹), hence measurable; Φ is κ-antilipschitz on Ω; A is Hⁿ-null-measurable; and p holds Hⁿ-a.e. on A ∩ Φ(Ω) because it holds Hⁿ-a.e. on A ⊇ A ∩ Φ(Ω) (`ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset`). The conclusion: D is Lⁿ-null-measurable, and p(Φ(w)) holds for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D.
2. (Rademacher.) h∘Φ is (L·K)-Lipschitz on Ω (`LipschitzWith.comp_lipschitzOnWith`). By Rademacher's theorem for maps Lipschitz on a set (Mathlib `LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem`), for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ ℝⁿ with w ∈ Ω, h∘Φ is differentiable within Ω at w. Since Ω is open (Ω ∈ 𝓝 w), h∘Φ is then differentiable at w (`DifferentiableWithinAt.differentiableAt`). Restricting to D ⊆ Ω (`ae_restrict_of_ae`): h∘Φ is differentiable at Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D.
3. Fix w ∈ D at which steps 1 and 2 hold; Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D qualifies, using also `ae_restrict_mem₀` to get w ∈ D. Let B := D(h∘Φ)(w) and x := Φ(w). Fix s ∈ ℝⁿ, and put u := A_w s ∈ range A_w and φ₂(t) := h(x + t·u).
(a) Applying p(x) to the point w itself, φ₂ has derivative ⟨G(x), A_w s⟩ at t = 0.
(b) φ₂ also has derivative Bs at t = 0. The line t ↦ w + ts has derivative s. By the chain rule (`HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt`), φ₁(t) := (h∘Φ)(w + ts) has derivative Bs at 0, and t ↦ Φ(w + ts) has derivative A_w s at 0, i.e. Φ(w + ts) − Φ(w) − tA_w s = o(t). Since h is L-Lipschitz,
|φ₂(t) − φ₁(t)| = |h(x + tA_w s) − h(Φ(w + ts))| ≤ L·|Φ(w + ts) − Φ(w) − tA_w s| = o(t).
As φ₂(0) = φ₁(0) = h(x),
φ₂(t) − φ₂(0) − t·Bs = [φ₁(t) − φ₁(0) − t·Bs] + [φ₂(t) − φ₁(t)] = o(t).
In Lean: `hasDerivAt_iff_isLittleO`, then `IsBigO.of_bound` with constant L, `IsBigO.trans_isLittleO`, `IsLittleO.add` and `IsLittleO.congr_left`.
(c) By uniqueness of derivatives (`HasDerivAt.unique`), Bs = ⟨G(x), A_w s⟩.
4. Since s was arbitrary, B = (innerSL ℝ (G(x))) ∘ A_w as continuous linear maps, and h∘Φ has Fréchet derivative B at w (`DifferentiableAt.hasFDerivAt`). This holds for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D. ∎
proof_key_steps: ae_pullback moves the tangential-derivative hypothesis from Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A to Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A).
Rademacher (LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem) for h∘Φ, which is Lipschitz on the open set Ω.
Directional derivative: t ↦ h(Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s) has derivative D(h∘Φ)(w)s, since it differs from (h∘Φ)(w + ts) by at most L·o(t).
Uniqueness of derivatives gives D(h∘Φ)(w)s = ⟨G(Φ(w)), DΦ(w)s⟩ for every s.

subproblem.title: Area formula on a bi-Lipschitz chart for Bochner integrals: ∫_A F dHⁿ = ∫_{Ω∩Φ⁻¹(A)} JΦ·F∘Φ dLⁿ
subproblem.statement: Let E be a real Banach space, P, n ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, and Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P Lipschitz on Ω and κ-antilipschitz on Ω for some κ > 0, i.e. κ|w − w'| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w')| for w, w' ∈ Ω. Let A ⊆ Φ(Ω) be Hⁿ-null-measurable and F : ℝ^P → E Hⁿ⌞A-integrable, where Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P and Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ. Put D := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A) and JΦ(w) := √det(⟨DΦ(w)e_i, DΦ(w)e_j⟩)_{i,j<n}, with DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w and e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1. Then D is Lⁿ-null-measurable, w ↦ JΦ(w)·F(Φ(w)) is Lⁿ-integrable on D, and ∫_A F dHⁿ = ∫_D JΦ(w)·F(Φ(w)) dLⁿ(w).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (the area formula on the chart, extended from nonnegative to signed integrands). Here F is any Banach-valued integrable function, which covers the real integrands of steps 8–9 and the vector field Y of step 8. The parent splits a real F into positive and negative parts; for Banach-valued F the same step is done once for the measures (step 4 below). Notation as in the statement; JΦ ≥ 0 because it is a square root.
1. (The nonnegative formula.) Apply the sibling chart_change_of_variables (lpf_raf_chart_change_of_variables) to the same Φ, Ω, A. For every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] that is Hⁿ⌞A-a.e. measurable: D is Lⁿ-null-measurable, g∘Φ is Lⁿ⌞D-a.e. measurable, and ∫⁻_A g dHⁿ = ∫⁻_D g(Φ(w))·ofReal(JΦ(w)) dw. With g = 0 this already gives the first conclusion: D is Lⁿ-null-measurable.
2. (JΦ is Borel.) w ↦ DΦ(w) is Borel measurable for every map Φ (Mathlib `measurable_fderiv`). The map Λ ↦ √det(⟨Λe_i, Λe_j⟩)_{i,j} is continuous on the space of linear maps ℝⁿ → ℝ^P: the entries are continuous, det is a polynomial and √ is continuous (`fun_prop` proves it). So JΦ is Borel, and so is w ↦ JΦ(w).toNNReal.
3. (A measure on the parameter side.) Let ρ := Lⁿ⌞D with density ofReal∘JΦ (Mathlib `withDensity` with density w ↦ ↑(JΦ(w).toNNReal), which is ofReal(JΦ(w)) by definition). Φ is continuous on Ω (it is Lipschitz there) and Ω is open, so Φ is Lⁿ⌞Ω-a.e. measurable (`ContinuousOn.aemeasurable`). Since D ⊆ Ω (`Measure.restrict_mono`), Φ is Lⁿ⌞D-a.e. measurable. Since ρ ≪ Lⁿ⌞D (`withDensity_absolutelyContinuous`), Φ is ρ-a.e. measurable.
4. (Φ pushes ρ forward to Hⁿ⌞A.) Let S ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel. Then:
(Φ_#ρ)(S) = ρ(Φ⁻¹(S)) (`Measure.map_apply_of_aemeasurable`)
= ∫⁻_{Φ⁻¹(S)} ofReal(JΦ) d(Lⁿ⌞D) (`withDensity_apply'`; Lⁿ⌞D is s-finite)
= ∫⁻_D 1_S(Φ(w))·ofReal(JΦ(w)) dw (`lintegral_indicator₀`; Φ⁻¹(S) is Lⁿ⌞D-null-measurable by step 3, and 1_{Φ⁻¹(S)}·ofReal(JΦ) = (1_S∘Φ)·ofReal(JΦ) pointwise)
= ∫⁻_A 1_S dHⁿ (step 1 with the Borel function g = 1_S)
= Hⁿ(S ∩ A) = (Hⁿ⌞A)(S).
Two measures that agree on all Borel sets are equal, so Φ_#ρ = Hⁿ⌞A.
5. (Transfer of integrability and integral.) F is Hⁿ⌞A-integrable, i.e. Φ_#ρ-integrable. Φ is ρ-a.e. measurable and F is Φ_#ρ-a.e. strongly measurable. Hence F∘Φ is ρ-integrable (`integrable_map_measure`), and ∫_A F dHⁿ = ∫ F d(Φ_#ρ) = ∫ F(Φ(w)) dρ(w) (`integral_map`).
6. (Removing the density.) Let f := JΦ.toNNReal : ℝⁿ → [0, ∞), which is Borel. For any G : ℝⁿ → E: G is ρ-integrable iff w ↦ f(w)·G(w) is Lⁿ⌞D-integrable (`integrable_withDensity_iff_integrable_smul`), and ∫ G dρ = ∫_D f(w)·G(w) dw (`integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul`). Because JΦ ≥ 0, f(w) = JΦ(w) as real numbers (`Real.coe_toNNReal`), so f(w)·G(w) = JΦ(w)·G(w) (`NNReal.smul_def`). Take G := F∘Φ. With step 5, w ↦ JΦ(w)·F(Φ(w)) is Lⁿ-integrable on D and ∫_A F dHⁿ = ∫_D JΦ(w)·F(Φ(w)) dw. ∎
proof_key_steps: chart_change_of_variables: D is null-measurable, and ∫⁻_A g dHⁿ = ∫⁻_D (g∘Φ)·JΦ dLⁿ for every measurable g ≥ 0.
JΦ is Borel (measurable fderiv composed with the continuous Gram-determinant map) and nonnegative.
With ρ := JΦ·Lⁿ⌞D, Φ is ρ-a.e. measurable and Φ_#ρ = Hⁿ⌞A (test on Borel sets with g = 1_S).
integral_map and integrable_map_measure transfer F to F∘Φ under ρ.
integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul and integrable_withDensity_iff_integrable_smul turn ρ back into JΦ·Lⁿ⌞D.

subproblem.title: An integrable tangent field on a chart piece lifts to an integrable coefficient field c with DΦ·c = JΦ·(Y∘Φ)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, and Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P of class C¹, Lipschitz on Ω and κ-antilipschitz on Ω for some κ > 0. Let A ⊆ Φ(Ω) be Hⁿ-null-measurable and Y : ℝ^P → ℝ^P Hⁿ⌞A-integrable, such that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A and every w ∈ Ω with Φ(w) = x, Y(x) ∈ range DΦ(w). Put D := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A) and JΦ(w) := √det(⟨DΦ(w)e_i, DΦ(w)e_j⟩)_{i,j<n}. Then there is c : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, Lⁿ-integrable on Ω, with c(w) = 0 for every w ∉ D and DΦ(w)c(w) = JΦ(w)·Y(Φ(w)) for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D. Here Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P, Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w and e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 8 of the parent proof, the coefficient field c = 1_{E'}·JΦ·a with a = (AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀ(Y∘Φ). Here the explicit left inverse (AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀ is replaced by the continuous left inverse Λ of the sibling continuous_left_inverse, which has exactly the properties used there. Notation as in the statement; A_w := DΦ(w).
1. (Left inverse.) The sibling continuous_left_inverse (lpf_tde_continuous_left_inverse) gives Λ : L(ℝⁿ, ℝ^P) → L(ℝ^P, ℝⁿ), continuous on the set of injective linear maps, such that every injective B satisfies Λ(B)∘B = id and |B(Λ(B)v)| ≤ |v| for all v ∈ ℝ^P.
2. (Chart derivative bounds.) Φ is C¹, so it is differentiable everywhere and w ↦ A_w is continuous (`ContDiff.continuous_fderiv`). For w ∈ Ω, the sibling fderiv_lower_bound (lpf_wtc_cat_fderiv_lower_bound) gives κ|s| ≤ |A_w s| for all s ∈ ℝⁿ. Consequences: A_w is injective for w ∈ Ω, since A_w s = A_w s' gives κ|s − s'| ≤ 0, so s = s'. And for v ∈ ℝ^P, κ|Λ(A_w)v| ≤ |A_w Λ(A_w)v| ≤ |v|, i.e. |Λ(A_w)v| ≤ κ⁻¹|v|.
3. (Integrability of Z.) Apply the sibling chart_integral_eq with E := ℝ^P and F := Y (Y is Hⁿ⌞A-integrable). It gives: D is Lⁿ-null-measurable, and Z(w) := JΦ(w)·Y(Φ(w)) is Lⁿ-integrable on D.
4. (Definition.) Put f(w) := Λ(A_w)(Z(w)) and c := 1_D·f, so c = f on D and c = 0 off D. In particular c(w) = 0 for every w ∉ D.
5. (c is integrable on Ω.) Measurability: w ↦ Λ(A_w) is continuous on Ω. It is the composition of the continuous map w ↦ A_w, which sends Ω into the injective maps by step 2, with Λ, which is continuous there. So it is Lⁿ⌞Ω-a.e. strongly measurable (Ω is open; `ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable`), hence Lⁿ⌞D-a.e. strongly measurable. Z is Lⁿ⌞D-a.e. strongly measurable by step 3, and evaluation (B, v) ↦ Bv is continuous bilinear, so f is Lⁿ⌞D-a.e. strongly measurable (`ContinuousLinearMap.aestronglyMeasurable_comp₂` with the identity of L(ℝ^P, ℝⁿ)).
Integrability: for every w ∈ D ⊆ Ω, |f(w)| ≤ κ⁻¹|Z(w)| by step 2, and κ⁻¹|Z| is integrable on D, so f is integrable on D (`Integrable.mono'`). D is null-measurable, so the extension by zero c = 1_D·f is Lⁿ-integrable on ℝⁿ (`IntegrableOn.integrable_indicator₀`), in particular on Ω.
6. (Pulling back the tangency.) Apply the sibling ae_pullback (lpf_ccr_ae_pullback) with M := A and p(x) := 'for every w ∈ Ω with Φ(w) = x, Y(x) ∈ range A_w'. subproblem.title: Tangential integrals over a chart piece as parameter integrals against one integrable field: ∫_A Df(Y) = ∫_Ω D(f∘Φ)(c) and ∫_A ⟨G, Y⟩ = ∫_Ω D(h∘Φ)(c)
subproblem.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open, and Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P of class C¹, Lipschitz on Ω and κ-antilipschitz on Ω for some κ > 0. Let A ⊆ Φ(Ω) be Hⁿ-null-measurable, h : ℝ^P → ℝ L-Lipschitz, G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P Borel with |G| ≤ L everywhere, and Y : ℝ^P → ℝ^P Hⁿ⌞A-integrable. Suppose that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A and every w ∈ Ω with Φ(w) = x: Y(x) ∈ range DΦ(w), and for every u ∈ range DΦ(w), s ↦ h(x + su) has derivative ⟨G(x), u⟩ at s = 0. Then there is c : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, Lⁿ-integrable on Ω, such that:
(i) ∫_A Df(x)(Y(x)) dHⁿ(x) = ∫_Ω D(f∘Φ)(w)(c(w)) dw for every differentiable f : ℝ^P → ℝ that is K-Lipschitz for some K ≥ 0;
(ii) ∫_A ⟨G(x), Y(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) = ∫_Ω D(h∘Φ)(w)(c(w)) dw.
Here D = fderiv ℝ, which is 0 where the map is not differentiable; DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w; Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P; and Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 9 of the parent proof, items (9a) and (9b): rewrite ∫_{M_j} F_k and ∫_{M_j} F_∞ as parameter integrals against the coefficient field. Steps 5, 7 and 8 of the parent are supplied by the three siblings. Notation: D := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A), A_w := DΦ(w), JΦ(w) := √det(⟨A_w e_i, A_w e_j⟩)_{i,j<n}. Φ is C¹, hence differentiable everywhere.
1. (Coefficient field.) Apply the sibling coefficient_field with the first half of the a.e. hypothesis (Y(x) ∈ range A_w). It gives c : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, Lⁿ-integrable on Ω, with c(w) = 0 for w ∉ D and A_w c(w) = JΦ(w)·Y(Φ(w)) for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D. This c is the field in the conclusion.
2. (Differential of h∘Φ.) Apply the sibling chart_has_fderiv_at with the second half of the a.e. hypothesis. It gives: for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D, h∘Φ has Fréchet derivative v ↦ ⟨G(Φ(w)), A_w v⟩ at w. In particular D(h∘Φ)(w)v = ⟨G(Φ(w)), A_w v⟩ (`HasFDerivAt.fderiv`).
3. (Integrals over Ω reduce to D.) For any u : ℝⁿ → ℝ and w ∈ Ω ∖ D we have c(w) = 0, so Du(w)(c(w)) = 0. Since Ω is measurable and D ⊆ Ω, ∫_Ω Du(w)(c(w)) dw = ∫_D Du(w)(c(w)) dw (`setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero`; no integrability is needed).
4. (Identity (i).) Let f be differentiable and K-Lipschitz, and put F(x) := Df(x)(Y(x)). F is Hⁿ⌞A-integrable:
- x ↦ Df(x) is Borel (`measurable_fderiv`), Y is Hⁿ⌞A-a.e. strongly measurable, and evaluation is continuous bilinear, so F is a.e. strongly measurable;
- |F(x)| ≤ ‖Df(x)‖·|Y(x)| ≤ K|Y(x)| (`norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz`), and K|Y| is integrable on A.
The sibling chart_integral_eq with E := ℝ gives ∫_A F dHⁿ = ∫_D JΦ(w)·F(Φ(w)) dw. For Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D (step 1), the chain rule (`fderiv_comp`; f is differentiable at Φ(w) and Φ at w) gives
D(f∘Φ)(w)(c(w)) = Df(Φ(w))(A_w c(w)) = Df(Φ(w))(JΦ(w)·Y(Φ(w))) = JΦ(w)·F(Φ(w)).
Hence ∫_D D(f∘Φ)(c) dLⁿ = ∫_D JΦ·(F∘Φ) dLⁿ (`integral_congr_ae`). With step 3, ∫_Ω D(f∘Φ)(w)(c(w)) dw = ∫_A F dHⁿ.
5. (Identity (ii).) Put F(x) := ⟨G(x), Y(x)⟩. F is Hⁿ⌞A-integrable: G is Borel, Y is a.e. strongly measurable and the inner product is continuous (`continuous_inner.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂`); and |F| ≤ |G|·|Y| ≤ L|Y|. chart_integral_eq gives ∫_A F dHⁿ = ∫_D JΦ(w)·F(Φ(w)) dw. For Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ D (steps 1 and 2),
D(h∘Φ)(w)(c(w)) = ⟨G(Φ(w)), A_w c(w)⟩ = ⟨G(Φ(w)), JΦ(w)·Y(Φ(w))⟩ = JΦ(w)·F(Φ(w)).
With step 3, ∫_Ω D(h∘Φ)(w)(c(w)) dw = ∫_D JΦ·(F∘Φ) dLⁿ = ∫_A ⟨G, Y⟩ dHⁿ. ∎
proof_key_steps: coefficient_field gives c integrable on Ω, c = 0 off D = Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(A), and DΦ(w)c(w) = JΦ(w)Y(Φ(w)) a.e. on D.
chart_has_fderiv_at gives D(h∘Φ)(w) = ⟨G(Φ(w)), DΦ(w)·⟩ a.e. on D.
∫_Ω Du(c) = ∫_D Du(c) because c = 0 on Ω ∖ D.
Chain rule: a.e. on D, D(f∘Φ)(w)(c(w)) = JΦ(w)·Df(Φ(w))(Y(Φ(w))) and D(h∘Φ)(w)(c(w)) = JΦ(w)·⟨G, Y⟩(Φ(w)).
chart_integral_eq (E = ℝ) turns ∫_D JΦ·(F∘Φ) back into ∫_A F dHⁿ for F = Df(Y) and F = ⟨G, Y⟩; both are dominated by a constant times |Y|.
